findings.item: Basis A: how memory was estimated (fitted to 4 GPU outputs)
findings.verdict: BASIS (fit computed from output files; every extrapolation below is an estimate)
findings.detail: Quantum ESPRESSO's 'Estimated max dynamical RAM' on 1 GPU (PAW 71/568 Ry, 3x3x1 k-points, 4 irreducible k) fits M ~ (V/V1) x (20.6 + 0.0637 x N_bands) GB. V1 = 25,140 bohr^3 is the 1 nm slab with 25 A vacuum. The fit reproduces all four measured values: 29.1 GB (1 nm, 15 A vacuum, 328 bands; model 29.4), 40.9 GB (1 nm vc-relax, 320 bands), 42.1 GB (1 nm IWO relax, 376 bands; model 44.6) and 82.1 GB (2 nm vc-relax, 672 bands; model 82.0). The 2 nm job at 82 GB ran on an H100 NVL with 93.6 GiB of GPU memory. The working rule is therefore: up to about 85 GB fits (there is a precedent), 85-100 GB is borderline and needs a dry run, and above 100 GB does not fit one GPU. Actual GPU memory use was never logged: NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. Measured host memory for 2 nm: 31 GB for the vc-relax and 66 GB for the final SCF. The other scaling inputs: plane waves scale with V (N_pw = V k^3 / 6 pi^2, which gives ~328,400 for the 2 nm cell at 71 Ry), and bands scale with electrons (In 13, O 6, W 14, H 1). For hybrid runs the exact-exchange (EXX) memory scales as N_occupied x V x number of k+q points. NC-PBE (80/320 Ry) needs about 2.2x less memory than PAW on the same 1 nm slab (18.8 vs 40.9 GB).
findings.evidence: PKG=...\IWO_PHYSICS_CONSTRAINED_MODEL_V1. qe_workflow/cern_htcondor/results/gpu_bench_v15/scf.out:47,51,485; results/slab1_relax_gpu/vcrelax.out:51,245; results/iwo_slab1_W24d_x1/relax.out:52,262 and iwo_slab1_W24d_x1_driver.log:3 (H100 NVL 95830 MiB); results/live_snapshots/slab2_relax_c2_vcrelax.out:47,50,51,321,325; RESULTS_LOG.md:10 (65.9 GB final SCF); results/nc_pbe_slab1_e80/scf.out:463

findings.item: Basis B: how wall time was estimated, and the GPU-vs-CPU factor
findings.verdict: BASIS (computed from output files; extrapolations are estimates)
findings.detail: Measured time per SCF iteration on one H100 NVL: 12.1 s (1 nm, 15 A vacuum, SCF), 15.0 s (1 nm IWO relax: 16,173 s over 1,078 iterations) and 40.5 s (2 nm vc-relax: 82,832 s over 2,045 iterations; 40 BFGS steps in 23.0 h, i.e. 33.7 min per step). Going from 96 to 176 atoms multiplied the time per iteration by 2.7, which is about N_atoms^1.6 or (V x N_bands)^1.2. For larger cells I use a range: t ~ (V x N_bands)^1.2 as the optimistic case and t ~ V x N_bands^2 (cubic) as the pessimistic case. Time is proportional to the number of irreducible k-points: 4 for the symmetric slabs, 5 for low-symmetry 3x3x1, 10 for 4x4x1 and 13 for 5x5x1. A relax needs 38-50 SCF iterations per BFGS step (measured). One H100 NVL is worth about 130 CPU cores on these slabs: 8.2x 16 cores at 96 atoms, and 162 s per iteration on 32 cores vs 40.5 s on the GPU at 176 atoms. A100 nodes ran about 2x slower than H100. Wall-time flavours: 8 h, 1 day, 3 days (testmatch) and 7 days (nextweek).
findings.evidence: results/gpu_bench_v15/scf.out:1791,2629; iwo_slab1_W24d_x1/relax.out (1,078 iterations, last 'total cpu time' 16,173 s; 'bfgs converged in 28 scf cycles and 27 bfgs steps'); live_snapshots/slab2_relax_c2_vcrelax.out (2,045 iterations, 82,831.9 s; line 52712 = BFGS step 39); results/cpu_relax_snapshots/slab2_relax_vcrelax.out (32 MPI, npool 2, 261 iterations in 42,369 s); report_latex_full/chapters/13_dft.tex:1328,1331; jobs/make_jobs.py:37-47 (flavours)

findings.item: Basis C: the measured HSE06 costs are mostly stress, not SCF
findings.verdict: COST CORRECTION (computed from output files)
findings.detail: The 4.0 h HSE06 run on the 1 nm slab spent 11,724 s (81 %) computing the exact-exchange stress. The stress is on because pw_input hard-codes tstress = .true.; the electronic part took 1,054 s. Bulk q=1: stress 542 s of 726 s. Bulk q=3: 13,500 s of 15,300 s. Without stress the costs are about 45 min (1 nm), about 3 min (bulk q=1) and about 30 min (bulk q=3), all on one H100 (estimated as total minus stress). Every hybrid single point (no relaxation) should set tstress = .false., which makes it about 5x cheaper. Memory: the default ecutfock gave 103.7 GB of EXX arrays (120 GB in total) and ran out of GPU memory; ecutfock 160 Ry gives 40.6 GB EXX / 58.4 GB total, which fits. The '9 min' PBE benchmark was the 15 A vacuum cell. The 25 A production 1 nm cell has 1.41x the dense G-vectors (5.75 M vs 4.08 M) and costs about 1.3x more per iteration.

findings.item: Pseudopotential inventory (Pd, Al, SG15 W)
findings.verdict: BLOCKER for items 11-16 and Block 2 (a download needs the user's approval)
findings.detail: qe_workflow/pseudo holds PAW In (dn), O (n), W (spn) and H, plus SG15 In, O, H and W. There is no Pd and no Al file, PAW or norm-conserving, anywhere in the handoff tree. So whether Pd carries 10 valence electrons (a 4d/5s data set) or 18 (with 4s4p semicore) is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA, and the estimates below give both. A 10-electron Pd set is recommended: it removes 8 e per Pd atom (416 e for 52 Pd, ~20 % of a Pd/2 nm model) and lowers the Pd/2 nm memory from ~136-154 GB to ~116-127 GB (estimate). Al is expected to have 3 valence electrons (not verified locally). The SG15 W file has z_valence = 28 (4f in valence), against 14 for PAW W, so HSE runs on W systems carry +14 e per W. Pd and Al files must be downloaded with the user's approval, as was done for SG15. The Pd lattice constant and Pd(001) work function must then be recomputed with the chosen file (<1 GPU-h or a few CPU core-h, estimate). Bader charges need the external 'bader' program, which is not in the package. Loewdin charges from projwfc.x are a no-cost substitute.

findings.item: Workflow limits: multi-GPU mode, ~25 h ticket, 7-day limit, PDOS of GPU runs
findings.verdict: CONSTRAINTS (code changes needed before any >1-GPU or >25 h item)
findings.detail: (1) The driver's multi-GPU mode runs 'pw.x -nk $NGPU', one k-point pool per GPU. Each pool holds complete wavefunctions, so the memory per GPU does not drop. Memory-bound systems (3 nm, Pd/2 nm, Al2O3/2 nm, HSE on 2 nm) need -nk 1 (plane-wave distribution across GPUs), which is untested in this container. A 2-GPU request waited 2.5 h in the queue, acceptable for jobs of 1-3 days. (2) The driver checkpoints to EOS only after a whole pw.x step, by xrdcp, which needs a valid ticket; output transfer is ON_EXIT. Every 2 nm-class relaxation (11-40 h), every 2-GPU interface relax (13-25 h wall), the 3 nm vc-relax (40-65 h) and AIMD (days) runs past the ~25 h ticket (all estimates). Fix: cap max_seconds at ≤20-22 h per pw.x step and chain continuations from the last geometry (qeio.py newgeom). Restarts lose the BFGS history; the 1 nm continuation needed 54 GPU steps after 13 CPU steps. HTCondor self-checkpointing is an alternative; whether CERN supports it is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. MD restarts need velocity/restart files, which the 15-min text snapshots do not carry. (3) projwfc.x cannot read GPU saves: dat2h5.py converts only the density, and the container has no pp.x or average.x (projwfc.x not recorded). STEPS_IWO_SLAB therefore runs the final SCF, PDOS and bands on 8 CPU cores inside the GPU job, with the GPU idle. For 2 nm IWO this is an estimated 11-16 h SCF + 2-4 h PDOS + 10-30 h bands, and the job can approach the 72 h testmatch limit. Every PDOS/LDOS item inherits a CPU SCF of ~100-500 core-h (estimate).
findings.evidence: jobs/common/driver.sh:76 (-np $NGPU ... -nk $NGPU), 84-99 (max_seconds, checkpoint after step), 34-38 (xrdcp checkpoint); jobs/common/jobs.sub:7 (ON_EXIT); jobs/make_jobs.py:57 (2-GPU idle 2.5 h), 192-203 (FORCE_CPU), 87 (iwo_slab2_W24d: 8 CPUs, 100 GB, testmatch); RESULTS_LOG.md:6-7,10; PROTOCOL_CERN.md:216; results/iwo_slab1_final_cpu/scf.out:2687 (1 nm CPU final SCF 2h55m on 16 cores)

findings.item: Item 1: relaxed 2 nm pristine In2O3 (PBE, plus HSE check)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE (PBE, running); the HSE part: see the 2 nm HSE06 item
findings.detail: 176 atoms (In56 O96 H24), 1,328 e, 672 bands (vc-relax) / 680 (final SCF). Memory 82 GB (QE estimate), host 31 GB measured (66 GB for the final SCF; 100 GB is now requested). Time: 68 steps x 33.7 min ~ 38 h on one H100 (estimate). 40 steps were done in 23.0 h, so ~16 h remain, then about 1 h for the final SCF and ~1.5 h for bands (estimate). Total for this relaxation ~40 GPU-h, of which ~20 GPU-h are still to come. The job passes the ~25 h ticket expiry at about step 43, so in-job EOS checkpoints will fail. The result depends on the HTCondor transfer at exit and on the laptop snapshot loop.

findings.item: Item 2: vacuum alignment for bulk, 1 nm and 2 nm (EA, IP, dEC, dEV)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE (post-processing only)
findings.detail: No new SCF is needed. EA and IP come from pp.x/average.x on the 1 nm save (slab1r_final_cpu, done) and the 2 nm save (in the chain). The bulk alignment uses the slab-interior macroscopic average plus the bulk 'VBM minus average potential' from a bulk pp.x run. Cost: ~0 GPU-h and <20 CPU core-h (estimate). The hybrid correction of the bulk edges can reuse the NC bulk PBE and HSE runs (pp.x on their saves, or re-runs without stress at ~3 min each). Results are labelled computed, not validated.

findings.item: Item 3: 2 nm IWO, W at the centre (24d)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: 176 atoms (In55 W O96 H24), 1,329 e (PAW), metallic. make_jobs passes no nbnd to the iwo_slab relax, so QE takes its smearing default of ~1.2 x 1329/2 ~ 798 bands; the 1 nm IWO run got 376, which matches that default. Memory would then be ~87-92 GB (estimate, above the 82 GB precedent), with a real risk of running out of GPU memory. Setting nbnd = occupied + 24 = 688 gives ~83 GB (estimate). Time: 25-40 BFGS steps x 28-35 min ~ 12-23 GPU-h (estimate). The FORCE_CPU final steps on 8 cores (SCF, PDOS, bands; see the limits item) add an estimated 25-50 h of idle-GPU wall time and can approach the 72 h limit. They should be split into a separate 16-32 core CPU job (~150-500 core-h, estimate).
findings.evidence: jobs/make_jobs.py:256-260 (relax.in written without nbnd), 87; iwo_slab1_W24d_x1/relax.out:51-52 (625 e -> 376 bands), 262; chains.txt:5 (fires automatically after slab2_relax)

findings.item: Items 4-5: 2 nm IWO, W subsurface and W at the surface (segregation energy, PDOS, Bader)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: Same size and electron count as item 3. An off-centre W breaks the z -> -z symmetry, which needs: a dipole correction (tefield/dipfield, never used in this workflow, GPU support untested), a vacuum of at least 15 A with a sawtooth region, and 5 irreducible k-points (+25 % time). Estimate: 25-40 steps x 35-44 min ~ 15-30 GPU-h per configuration, <25 h only at the low end. The H-passivated surface is not the device's air, Pd or Al2O3 interface, so E_seg has limited meaning. Cheapest adequate route: a 1 nm pilot for W at the surface vs the centre (96 atoms, ~42-45 GB, ~5-7 GPU-h each, estimate), then a single 2 nm off-centre configuration. Alternative: a symmetric W pair keeps the z-flip symmetry (no dipole correction) at 2 W (~3.6 %).
findings.evidence: jobs/make_jobs.py:256-260; structures_v2/build_iwo_slab.py:33-40 (z-flip check, dipole_correction_needed); grep: no tefield/dipfield anywhere in cern_htcondor; results/iwo_slab1_W24d_x1_driver.log:5 (1 nm relax 4h29m)

findings.item: Items 6-8: 2 nm V_O in the interior, subsurface and at the surface (neutral)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: 175 atoms (In56 O95 H24), 1,322 e. Set nbnd explicitly (~677) and use smearing; memory ~82-83 GB (estimate, borderline, as for 2 nm). The two off-centre positions need the dipole correction. Estimate: 20-40 steps x 34-42 min ~ 11-28 GPU-h each, so 33-84 GPU-h for all three, plus an O2 reference (<1 GPU-h). The proposal's 'bulk V_O^q first' is also the cheapest step. 80-atom bulk V_O at charges 0, +1 and +2: 698/697/696 e, ~14 GB, about 4-10 GPU-h each for a PBE relax (estimate), or about a day each on 32 CPU cores (the W24d relax took 23h48m). HSE single points on the 80-atom cell: ~29-46 GB, 1-3 GPU-h each with stress off (estimate). Then a 1 nm pilot for the positions (5-7 GPU-h each) and 2 nm only for the 1-2 lowest-energy configurations. Charged defects in vacuum slabs stay postponed, as proposed.

findings.item: Items 9-10: 2 nm W+V_O, adjacent and separated (binding energy)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES (adjacent); NOT ADEQUATE as specified (separated)
findings.detail: 175 atoms (In55 W O95 H24), 1,323 e: 11-28 GPU-h per configuration (estimate). In a 10.3 A in-plane cell the largest W-V_O separation is about 7-10 A, so 'separated' is not a dilute reference, and E_bind = E(W) + E(V_O) - E(W+V_O) - E(pristine) mixes in image interactions. Cheapest adequate route: E_bind in bulk. The 80-atom cell (max separation ~8.9 A, ~14 GB, 4-10 GPU-h per configuration) or a rebuilt 160-atom 1x1x2 cell (~44 GB, 8-16 GPU-h) both fit one GPU. Then compute one adjacent configuration in the 2 nm slab. The old qe_workflow/bulk_IWO_1W_1p6pct_112 inputs predate the rebuilt structures and must not be reused.

findings.item: (c) Lattice-matched Pd / In2O3(001) supercell
findings.verdict: Pd(001) sqrt13 x sqrt13 R33.7 deg: FEASIBLE; Pd(111): NOT FEASIBLE
findings.detail: Geometry computed here from the given lattice constants. The In2O3(001) cell is square: 10.306 A (PBE bulk) or 10.336 x 10.335 A (relaxed 1 nm slab). The Pd(001) surface net is square with a_s = a/sqrt2 = 2.751 A (a = 3.89 A, experimental). A literature-typical PBE a of ~3.94-3.95 A (not computed here) gives a_s ~ 2.79 A. Options on the 1x1 oxide cell: (i) Pd(001) sqrt13 x sqrt13 R33.7 deg, the (3,2) vector, 9.918 A (exp.) / ~10.05-10.07 A (PBE). Pd is stretched +3.9 to +4.2 % (exp. a) or +2.3 to +2.9 % (PBE a), with 13 Pd per layer. This is the recommended cell. (ii) Pd(001) 4x4, 11.00 A: compressed -6.1 to -6.3 % (exp.) or -7.3 to -7.8 % (PBE), 16 Pd per layer. (iii) sqrt17: -9 %. Pd(111) is hexagonal (a_h = 2.751 A) on a square cell. The best small rectangular cell, 4 x 2sqrt3 (16 Pd per layer), has anisotropic strain of -6.3 % / +8.2 %. Rotated sqrt13 hexagonal vectors give 60 deg cells, and sqrt13 x sqrt39 gives a 20 % mismatch. Strain below 1 % first appears at 15 a_h ~ 4 x 10.31 A and 13 sqrt3 a_h ~ 6 x 10.31 A, i.e. a 4x6 oxide supercell (>4,000 atoms for a 2 nm film), which is not feasible. Layers: Pd(001) interlayer spacing a/2 = 1.945 A; 4/5/6 layers = 52/65/78 Pd. Four layers is the cheapest acceptable choice; test it against 6 on the pilot through the work function (<2 GPU-h, estimate). The texture of the device's Pd film is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA, so the facet is a model choice. Report the facet dependence of the barrier as a systematic uncertainty rather than computing it.
findings.evidence: RESULTS_LOG.md:73 (10.336 x 10.335 A); PROTOCOL_CERN.md:90 (a = 10.3061 A); report 03_device_data.tex:59 (Pd 70 nm top contacts)

findings.item: Items 11-13: Pd on 2 nm In2O3, Pd on 2 nm IWO, Pd on 2 nm IWO + interfacial V_O
findings.verdict: Relaxed at 2 nm: NOT FEASIBLE on 1 GPU (FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES on 2 GPUs); 1 nm pilot: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: Model: Pd(001) sqrt13, 4 layers (52 Pd). The oxide side is O-terminated (top 12 H removed). Dipole correction, MV smearing, nbnd ~1.15-1.2 x occupied, 3x3x1 k (5 irreducible) for the relaxation and 4x4x1 (10 k) for the final SCF and LDOS. [P1] Pd on 1 nm IWO: 136 atoms. 1,132 e / ~650 bands with 10-e Pd, or 1,548 e / ~890 bands with 18-e Pd. c ~34-36 A. Memory ~64 GB (10-e Pd) or ~77 GB (18-e Pd), estimate; fits one H100. Host memory ~45 GB for 10 k-points (estimate). Time per iteration ~36 s at 5 k and ~72 s at 10 k (estimate). Relax: 30-50 steps ~ 6-15 h, plus the final SCF/pp/PDOS ~1.5-2.5 h, so 8-17 GPU-h per configuration (estimate), each under 25 h. [P2] Pd on 2 nm IWO: 216 atoms (229 with 5 layers). 1,836 e / ~1,055 bands with 10-e Pd, or 2,252 e / ~1,300 bands with 18-e Pd. c ~46-48 A. Memory ~116-127 GB (10-e) or ~136-154 GB (18-e), estimate; does not fit one H100. It needs 2 H100 with -nk 1 (~60-80 GB per GPU, estimate) or a ~200 GB CPU job. Time per iteration ~89 s at 5 k and ~178 s at 10 k, 1-GPU equivalent (estimate). Relax: ~25-45 GPU-h on 2 GPUs (estimate), 13-25 h wall. A single-point SCF+pp+PDOS on a geometry transferred from P1: ~5-9 GPU-h. Each drho(z) needs two extra frozen-geometry SCFs: +1-2 GPU-h (P1) or +4-8 (P2). A lateral registry scan of ≥3 starting positions adds ~12-18 GPU-h at P1. Phi_Bn in a 1 nm film has no bulk-like interior, so E_C must come from layer-resolved LDOS plus bulk alignment. Correct the CB edge with the bulk HSE-PBE shift (Pd HSE is not feasible).
findings.evidence: Memory/time model (Basis A, B); jobs/common/driver.sh:76; pseudo inventory (no Pd); 12_conclusions.tex:88

findings.item: Block 2: Pd/V_O mini-campaign (6 interface models)
findings.verdict: As written (2 nm, relaxed): NOT FEASIBLE on 1 GPU; FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES on the 1 nm pilot
findings.detail: As written: 6 x 25-45 GPU-h, plus a registry scan (30-45) and drho subsystems (10-20), ~190-335 GPU-h (estimate). All of it needs 2 GPUs with -nk 1 and the Pd download. Cheapest adequate route: run all six on P1 (6 x 8-17 GPU-h + registry 12-18 + drho 3-6, ~65-125 GPU-h, estimate, each job <25 h on 1 GPU). Then run 2 nm single points for pristine and the lowest-energy V_O (2 x 5-9 GPU-h on 2 GPUs). Caveat: in a 1 nm film the 'channel centre' V_O is only ~0.5 nm from Pd. The quoted thermionic factors are arithmetically correct: exp(0.1/0.02585) = 47.8 and exp(0.2/0.02585) = 2.29e3 (computed). Carrying a DFT Phi_Bn into ATLAS needs new launches: 57 of 57 are used, so this needs the user's approval.

findings.item: (d) Al2O3 / IWO interface options and items 14-15
findings.verdict: alpha/gamma crystalline: NOT FEASIBLE (strain); amorphous Al2O3 on 1 nm IWO: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES; on 2 nm IWO: needs 2 GPUs
findings.detail: No crystalline option matches the square 10.31-10.34 A cell. alpha-Al2O3(0001) is hexagonal (a = 4.759 A, literature value); the rectangular 2a x a sqrt3 cell is 9.52 x 8.24 A, a mismatch of +8.3 % / +25 %, and an exact coincidence needs a 4x6 oxide supercell. The r-plane (~4.76 x 5.13 A, literature-typical) in 2x2 gives +8.3 % / +0.5 % anisotropic strain. gamma-Al2O3 is a defect spinel (a ~7.9 A); its (001) sqrt2 x sqrt2 R45 deg cell is 11.2 A (-8 %), and the vacancy disorder needs several models. Amorphous Al2O3 adopts the oxide's in-plane cell (no strain) and matches the 2 nm ALD layer. At 3.0 g/cm^3 (literature-typical ALD density, not measured here) and 106.8 A^2 of area, 1 nm = 19 Al2O3 = 95 atoms and 2 nm = 190 atoms (computed). [A1] 1 nm a-Al2O3 on 1 nm IWO plus ~10 H: ~189 atoms, ~1,078 e, ~555 bands, ~59-64 GB (estimate; fits). Relax 40-80 steps ~ 9-19 h + ~1 h final, i.e. 10-20 GPU-h (estimate). [A2] 1 nm a-Al2O3 on 2 nm IWO: ~269 atoms, ~1,782 e, ~105 GB (estimate); 2 GPUs, 25-50 GPU-h. [A3] 2 nm a-Al2O3 on 2 nm IWO: ~364 atoms, ~2,238 e, ~150 GB (estimate); NOT FEASIBLE on 1 GPU. The amorphous Al2O3 can be generated by MLIP or classical MD (≤1-3 GPU-h) or by AIMD of a 95-atom bulk-like cell (Gamma-only, ~8-22 GPU-h, estimate). At least 2-3 samples are needed. Item 15 (+V_O): 10-20 GPU-h per site at A1. The Al pseudopotential must be downloaded (approval needed).
findings.evidence: Memory/time model (Basis A, B); 04_derivations_electrostatics.tex:48 (Al2O3 2 nm in the stack); pseudo inventory (no Al)

findings.item: Item 16: full local stack Pd / IWO / Al2O3
findings.verdict: Relaxed: NOT FEASIBLE; single point: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES (2-4 GPUs)
findings.detail: Pd (4 layers) / 2 nm IWO / 1 nm a-Al2O3 + H: ~309 atoms, ~2,290 e with 10-e Pd, ~1,320 bands, c ~55 A, ~165 GB (estimate). It needs 2-3 or more H100 with -nk 1, or a ~250 GB CPU job. Being metallic it needs 4x4x1 k: ~290-475 s per iteration (1-GPU equivalent), ~4-10 GPU-h per SCF, and 100-500 GPU-h for a relaxation (estimate), multi-day and past the ticket expiry. Cheapest adequate route: one single-point SCF with V(z) and LDOS(z) on a geometry assembled from the relaxed P1/P2 and A1/A2 sub-interfaces, ~10-20 GPU-h (estimate). Lower priority than the two separate interfaces.

findings.item: (e) Items 17-19: amorphous 2 nm IWO, AIMD melt-quench vs MLIP
findings.verdict: AIMD x3: NOT FEASIBLE within the constraints (one reference structure only: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES); MLIP + DFT: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: AIMD on ~176 atoms with Gamma-only (about 4x fewer k and 1.5-2x from real wavefunctions) and ~50/400 Ry (0.59x the plane waves): ~3-4 s per SCF iteration and 6-12 iterations per MD step gives ~20-45 s per step (estimate). Smearing is required while molten. With H present the time step is ≤1 fs (~1-1.5 fs with deuterium mass). 10-15 ps then takes 10,000-15,000 steps, ~50-190 GPU-h per structure (estimate), so 150-570 GPU-h for three, plus 11-28 GPU-h each for the PBE relax at production settings. Each run lasts 2-8 days, past the 25 h ticket and near or over the 7-day limit. A restart loses the velocities, and the 10.3 A lateral cell imposes artificial periodicity. Melting a bulk-like cell without vacuum and cleaving it afterwards is ~2x cheaper. MLIP route: a universal pretrained MLIP melt-quench takes minutes to hours per structure, also in 2x2 lateral cells (~700 atoms) with slower quenches. DFT validation needs 5-10 single points (~1 GPU-h each). Then 3-5 samples get a short DFT relax (fmax ~0.05 eV/A, ~10-20 GPU-h each) plus PDOS and IPR, for an estimated 40-100 GPU-h in total. Downloading MLIP software and weights needs the user's approval. Pre-register the MLIP acceptance (force error, RDF against one AIMD or DFT reference). Suitable published classical In-W-O potentials: NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA.
findings.evidence: Per-iteration basis from live_snapshots/slab2_relax_c2_vcrelax.out; PROTOCOL_CERN.md:3 (PAW minimum cutoffs In 41/212, O 47/323, W 50/475 Ry); RESULTS_LOG.md:6-7 (ticket); jobs/make_jobs.py:47 (7-day flavour)

findings.item: Item 20: amorphous 2 nm IWO + V_O
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES
findings.detail: In an amorphous film V_O has many inequivalent sites, so one configuration says little. Screen all O sites with the MLIP (negligible cost), then run DFT relaxes on 2-3 sites (lowest energy plus representative), at 11-28 GPU-h each, ~30-80 GPU-h in total (estimate). As written (AIMD structures, arbitrary sites) the cost is ~30-90 GPU-h with weak statistics.

findings.item: Item 21: ~3 nm pristine film (bridge point)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES (2 GPUs), optional
findings.detail: n = 3 conventional cells: 256 atoms (In88 O144 H24), 2,032 e, ~1,024 bands, ~3.05 nm H to H (computed from 0.988 and 2.018 nm). Memory ~136 GB with 25 A vacuum, or ~112 GB with 15 A (estimate). 15 A is allowed for symmetric slabs because EA and IP changed by ≤0.1 meV between 15 and 35 A. It does not fit one H100 and needs 2 with -nk 1. Time per iteration ~86-116 s (1-GPU equivalent). A vc-relax from scratch (60-70 steps) costs 72-135 GPU-h (estimate). The cheapest adequate route inserts one bulk cell into the relaxed 2 nm slab and runs a fixed-cell relax of 15-25 steps, ~16-38 GPU-h on 2 GPUs and 10-25 h wall (estimate). The old qe_workflow/slab_3p0nm_* inputs use an older recipe (H16 In96 O144) and are not reusable.

findings.item: Item 22: second W concentration
findings.verdict: Higher W (2 W in 2 nm): FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES; lower W in a slab: NOT FEASIBLE; bulk 160-atom: FEASIBLE
findings.detail: 2 W in the 2 nm slab (In54 W2 O96 H24, 1,330 e, ~3.6 %) costs the same as item 3: 12-23 GPU-h with explicit nbnd (estimate). A lower W fraction in a slab needs a 2x1 or sqrt2 lateral cell (~352 atoms, >160 GB, estimate), which is not feasible. The cheapest adequate test of concentration dependence (W 5d position, E_F) is a 160-atom bulk cell (In63 W O96, 1,409 e, 1.6 % W, ~44 GB, 8-16 GPU-h, or ~2 days on 32 CPU cores, estimate), rebuilt from the relaxed bulk.

findings.item: (b) HSE06 on the 2 nm slab
findings.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE on 1 H100 as configured; FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES; recommended: skip
findings.detail: Setup as for 1 nm: SG15 at 80 Ry, ecutfock 160 Ry, q = 1, 3x3x1. EXX memory ~40.6 GB x (664/312 occupied) x 1.293 (volume) ~ 112 GB (estimate). Non-EXX NC memory ~48 GB, scaled from 18.8 GB at 1 nm (estimate). Total ~160 GB, against 93.6 GiB available. If memory were solved, the time without stress would be ~45 min x (664/312)^2 x 1.293 ~ 4.4 h (1-GPU equivalent, estimate). With the current tstress = .true. the EXX stress alone would add ~19 h. Options: (i) 2 H100 with -nk 1 (~80 GB per GPU, ~2.5-3 h wall, ~5-6 GPU-h, estimate); (ii) ecutfock 80 Ry (EXX x0.35, ~88 GB in total, borderline; needs a bulk + 1 nm ecutfock test of ~1 GPU-h); (iii) a 160-200 GB CPU job on 80-100 cores in the 10-slot large-core pool; (iv) skip. The protocol already allows applying the 1 nm ratio (1.06-1.11) to dEg(t). At 2 nm that correction is 0.02-0.04 eV on +0.33 eV (provisional), below what this item could resolve.

findings.item: HSE06 selection ('5-7 decisive systems')
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES (swap the 2 nm and interface systems for bulk and 1 nm equivalents)
findings.detail: Bulk pristine and 1 nm pristine are done. The 2 nm pristine run: see the 2 nm HSE06 item. 2 nm W (SG15 W = 28 e, 1,343 e, metallic): EXX ~115 GB + ~49 GB, so not on one GPU. Replace it with the 1 nm W slab (639 e, ~42 GB EXX + ~19 GB, ~61 GB, ~1-3 GPU-h with stress off) and the 80-atom bulk W24d cell (~29-46 GB, ~1-4 GPU-h; estimates). W 5d is a local property, already seen in bulk. Key V_O and W+V_O: in 80-atom bulk this fits (~1-4 GPU-h per single point); at 2 nm it does not fit one GPU. An HSE relax of an 80-atom defect, if localisation demands it, takes ~10-30 GPU-h per charge state (estimate). Pd interface: NOT FEASIBLE. There is no SG15 Pd, the system is metallic, and the EXX for Pd on 1 nm at 4x4x1 is ~200+ GB (estimate). Use PBE plus the bulk HSE-PBE band-edge shift, as the proposal says. Recommended HSE programme: 6-8 single points, ~6-25 GPU-h (estimate). HSE effective masses need Wannier interpolation; non-SCF hybrid bands are unavailable in pw.x.

findings.item: (a) 6.3 nm slab with the same recipe (n = 6)
findings.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE (1 GPU, 94 GB)
findings.detail: Computed from the recipe: 1x1x6 conventional cell = 192 In + 288 O; removing 8 In and adding 24 H gives 496 atoms (In184 O288 H24), 4,144 e, 2,072 occupied, ~2,080 bands (occupied + 8), ~6.14 nm H to H (estimate). The electron count closes: 3 x 184 + 24 = 576 = 2 x 288. Memory ~379 GB with 25 A vacuum, ~335 GB with 15 A (estimate), so at least 4-5 H100 with -nk 1. On CPUs it is ~142 GB per k-pool (scaled from 24 GB per pool at 2 nm), needing ~72+ cores in the large-core pool. Time per iteration ~340-740 s (1-GPU equivalent). One SCF costs 6-19 GPU-h-equivalent. A fixed-cell relax (15-25 steps) costs 57-200, a vc-relax 230-860 (estimates). Adding W or V_O means more relaxations of the same size. Even a single point needs a 4-5 GPU job or a 150-300 GB CPU job of 10-35 h on 64-72 cores (estimate). Cheapest adequate alternative: see the thickness matrix item.
findings.evidence: PROTOCOL_CERN.md:24-25,91,96 (recipe, thicknesses, 24 GB per pool); Basis A, B

findings.item: (a) 13.2 nm slab with the same recipe (n = 13)
findings.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE
findings.detail: Computed: 1056 atoms (In408 O624 H24), 9,072 e, ~4,544 bands, ~13.35 nm H to H (estimate). Electron count: 3 x 408 + 24 = 1248 = 2 x 624. Memory ~1.41 TB with 25 A vacuum, ~1.32 TB with 15 A (estimate). CPU ~570 GB per pool. Time per iteration ~0.5-1.8 h (1-GPU equivalent). One SCF costs 30-160 GPU-h-equivalent on 16-18 or more GPUs (estimate). No relaxation is possible within the 7-day limit.

findings.item: Thickness matrix (1 / 2 / 6.3 / 13.2 nm)
findings.verdict: 1 nm: FEASIBLE; 2 nm: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES; 6.3 and 13.2 nm: NOT FEASIBLE (replace with cheaper adequate methods)
findings.detail: 1 nm: every proposed system fits one GPU (96-189 atoms, ~41-80 GB, 5-20 GPU-h each, estimate). 2 nm: pristine, W, V_O and W+V_O fit at ~82-92 GB only with explicit nbnd. Pd, Al2O3, the full stack and HSE need 2 or more GPUs (-nk 1). 6.3 and 13.2 nm: see the two items above. The question 'are Eg, E_C and m* the same at 6.3 and 13.2 nm' does not need these slabs. The report already bounds the crystalline confinement beyond ~3 nm by an infinite well (12_conclusions.tex:97), and the fitted law gives dEc(6.3) = 0.07 eV against the ≥0.20 eV needed (12_conclusions.tex:88). The cheapest adequate route: bulk PBE/HSE bands plus an effective-mass or Wannier quantum-well model calibrated on the 1, 2 (and optional 3) nm DFT points. A pre-registered k-mesh test (3x3x1 vs shifted 2x2x1) on the 1 nm slab (~10 min per SCF) could halve the cost of any thick slab. The Pd barrier of a thick film is the P1/P2 interface dipole plus bulk alignment through the macroscopic average, so no thick slab is needed. The structural-transition hypothesis needs GIXRD/TEM data and amorphous or nanocrystalline MLIP models, not crystalline slabs.

findings.item: Budget: realistic core campaign (cheapest adequate version of items 1-22 plus Block 2)
findings.verdict: FEASIBLE: ~270-560 H100 GPU-h (estimate), ~340-840 with contingency
findings.detail: Estimates per block: item 1 finish ~20; item 2 ~0; item 3 12-23; W segregation (1 nm pilot + one 2 nm) 20-37; V_O (bulk V_O^q PBE 12-30 + HSE 3-12 + 1 nm pilot 15-21 + 2 nm for 1-2 configurations 11-56) 41-119; W+V_O (bulk + one 2 nm) 19-48; Pd (bulk Pd/WF + six P1 models + registry + drho + two 2 nm single points) 75-145; a-Al2O3/1 nm (+V_O) 21-43; amorphous via MLIP (+V_O) 50-100; bulk 160-atom W 8-16; HSE extras 2-7. Total ~270-560 GPU-h; with the optional 3 nm, +16-38. Adding a 25-50 % failure and requeue contingency gives ~340-840 GPU-h; for reference, ~50 of the 85-90 GPU-h used so far were lost to faults that are now fixed. CPU: ~2,000-8,000 core-h, mostly CPU-side PDOS SCFs and bulk relaxations, unless projwfc.x can read GPU saves. With 2-3 concurrent 1-GPU jobs this is ~1-3 weeks of running. A minimal decisive subset (items 1 and 3; bulk V_O^q with HSE; Pd/1 nm pristine + interfacial V_O; a-Al2O3/1 nm; MLIP amorphous with one validated sample) costs ~110-200 GPU-h (estimate). The ATLAS follow-up needs launches beyond 57 of 57.
findings.evidence: Item estimates above; 13_dft.tex:1447-1448 (usage and losses); config/solver.yaml:18

findings.item: Budget: the proposal as written
findings.verdict: NOT FEASIBLE as written
findings.detail: Estimates. Items 1-10 with full 2 nm relaxations: 117-243 GPU-h. Items 11-13 relaxed at 2 nm on 2 GPUs: 117-204. The other four 2 nm Pd models of Block 2: 100-180. Items 14-15 at 2 nm: 50-100. Item 16 relaxed: 100-500. Items 17-19 AIMD + PBE: 183-654. Item 20: 33-84. Item 21 vc-relax: 80-135. Item 22: 12-23. HSE on 5-7 systems including 2 nm and 2 nm W: 14-28. The 6.3 nm row (pristine, W, V_O on ≥5 GPUs): 195-720. Total ~1,000-2,900 GPU-h, i.e. 11-33x the GPU use to date, and the 13.2 nm row cannot be computed at all. Many jobs need 2-16 GPUs, run 1-8 days (past the 25 h ticket), and need Pd, Al and MLIP downloads.

top_recommendations: Before the chained 2 nm IWO job fires, set nbnd explicitly in the iwo_slab relax (occupied + 24, about 688). The current default, about 798 bands, gives an estimated 87-92 GB, against the 82 GB that is known to fit one H100 NVL (make_jobs.py:256-260, chains.txt:5). Move the FORCE_CPU final SCF, PDOS and bands into a separate 16-32 core CPU job so the GPU does not sit idle for an estimated 25-50 h.

Set tstress = .false. for every hybrid single point: 81 % of the 4.0 h for the 1 nm HSE06 run was exact-exchange stress (nc_hse_slab1_f160_e80/scf.out:5937,5939). Drop the 2 nm HSE06 check: it does not fit one GPU (estimated ~112 GB EXX + ~48 GB), and the protocol already allows applying the 1 nm ratio of 1.06-1.11. Spend the hybrid budget on bulk 80-atom V_O and W cells and on the 1 nm W slab (each estimated 1-4 GPU-h on one GPU).

Do not build 6.3 nm (496 atoms, ~379 GB) or 13.2 nm (1056 atoms, ~1.4 TB) slabs (estimates). Use the infinite-well bound already in the report (12_conclusions.tex:97), bulk band structure plus a quantum-well model calibrated on the 1, 2 (and optional 3) nm DFT points, and bulk alignment for thick-film Pd barriers.

Pd contacts: with the user's approval, download a Pd PAW file (prefer the 10-electron set) and an Al file; none exists locally. Use Pd(001) sqrt13 x sqrt13 R33.7 deg (13 Pd per layer, +2.3 to +2.9 % strain at PBE a, +3.9 to +4.2 % at experimental a), 4 layers, with dipole correction. Pd(111) needs a 4x6 oxide supercell for strain below 1 %. Run the whole Block 2 mini-campaign on the 1 nm IWO pilot (136 atoms, ~64 GB, estimated 8-17 GPU-h per configuration), then only 1-2 single points at 2 nm on 2 GPUs.

Change the driver's multi-GPU mode from '-nk $NGPU' to '-nk 1' (driver.sh:76) before any job above ~90 GB (3 nm, Pd/2 nm, Al2O3/2 nm, HSE at 2 nm). Today a 2-GPU job duplicates the wavefunctions and gains no memory. Test it once on the 2 nm slab.

Al2O3: use amorphous Al2O3, which takes the oxide's in-plane cell without strain (~95 atoms per nm), on the 1 nm IWO slab (~189 atoms, ~59-64 GB, estimated 10-20 GPU-h). alpha- and gamma-Al2O3 do not match the square 10.3 A cell (+8 to +25 % or -8 %).

Amorphous IWO: use a validated MLIP melt-quench followed by DFT short relaxes (estimated 40-100 GPU-h) rather than three AIMD runs (estimated 150-570 GPU-h, multi-day and fragile to restart). Pre-register the MLIP acceptance tests; the software download needs the user's approval.

Make long jobs survive the ~25 h ticket expiry: cap each pw.x step at 20-22 h with max_seconds and chain continuations with qeio.py newgeom (or verify HTCondor self-checkpointing at CERN). Keep the 15-min snapshot loop, and log nvidia-smi memory.used to calibrate the memory model.

Pre-register cheap tests before scaling up: dipole correction on the GPU build (1 nm W-surface slab), the k-mesh for metallic interfaces (3x3x1, 4x4x1 and 5x5x1 on the Pd pilot), 4 vs 6 Pd layers, sqrt13 vs 4x4 strain sensitivity of Phi_Bn, and a 3x3x1 vs shifted 2x2x1 test for thick slabs.

Budget the realistic core campaign at about 270-560 H100 GPU-h (about 340-840 with a 25-50 % failure contingency) plus 2,000-8,000 CPU core-h (estimates). A minimal decisive subset costs about 110-200 GPU-h. Any TCAD use of a DFT Phi_Bn needs ATLAS launches beyond 57 of 57, so the user must approve it.
summary:
Read-only compute-feasibility review of the proposed DFT campaign. PKG = C:\Users\moham\Downloads\IWO_Local_Codex_Handoff (1)\IWO_PHYSICS_CONSTRAINED_MODEL_V1; file paths in the findings are relative to PKG/qe_workflow/cern_htcondor unless stated. All numbers beyond the measured ones are estimates. Memory comes from a fit to four measured QE estimates on one GPU, M ~ (V/V1)(20.6 + 0.0637 N_bands) GB, which reproduces 29.1, 40.9, 42.1 and 82.1 GB. Time comes from measured per-iteration costs (12.1, 15.0 and 40.5 s on an H100 NVL), scaled between (V x N_bands)^1.2 and V x N_bands^2 and multiplied by the irreducible k count; one H100 is about 130 CPU cores.

Two corrections to the measured costs. First, the 4.0 h HSE06 run on the 1 nm slab was 81 % exact-exchange stress, because tstress = .true. is hard-coded; without stress it takes about 45 min. Second, the 9-min PBE benchmark used the 15 A vacuum cell, and the 25 A production cell costs about 1.3x more.

Hard limits on one 94 GB GPU:
- Up to 2 nm the pristine, W, V_O and W+V_O slabs fit (82-92 GB), but only with nbnd set explicitly. The pending 2 nm IWO job would run with the default, about 798 bands, which is borderline at an estimated 87-92 GB.
- These do not fit one GPU: 3 nm (256 atoms, ~112-136 GB), Pd on 2 nm (216-229 atoms, ~116-154 GB), Al2O3 on 2 nm (~105-150 GB), the full stack (~165 GB) and HSE06 on 2 nm (~112 GB EXX + ~48 GB).
- 6.3 nm (496 atoms, 4,144 e, ~379 GB) and 13.2 nm (1056 atoms, 9,072 e, ~1.4 TB) do not fit any single GPU job; 13.2 nm is out of reach entirely.
- The driver's multi-GPU mode uses one k-pool per GPU, which gives no memory relief; it must be changed to -nk 1.
- No Pd or Al pseudopotential exists locally, so the Pd valence (10 vs 18 e) is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. SG15 W has 28 valence electrons.
- Jobs longer than ~25 h lose their in-job EOS checkpoints.
- PDOS of GPU runs needs a duplicate CPU SCF.

Geometry: Pd(001) sqrt13 x sqrt13 R33.7 deg (13 Pd per layer, +2.3 to +4.2 % strain) is the only acceptable small Pd cell; Pd(111) needs a 4x6 oxide supercell. For Al2O3 only the amorphous form is lattice-compatible (about 95 atoms per nm). For amorphous IWO, MLIP followed by DFT is about 4-6x cheaper than three AIMD runs and more robust.

Classification:
- FEASIBLE: items 1 and 2, the 1 nm row, bulk V_O^q and bulk W+V_O.
- FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES: items 3-10, 1 nm Pd and Al2O3 pilots, 2 nm Pd single points on 2 GPUs, 3 nm on 2 GPUs, MLIP amorphous, and the HSE selection moved to bulk and 1 nm.
- NOT FEASIBLE: relaxed 2 nm Pd/Al2O3 and the capstone on one GPU, Pd(111), crystalline Al2O3, 6.3 and 13.2 nm slabs, HSE on 2 nm or interfaces on one GPU, and three AIMD structures.

Budget: a realistic core campaign is about 270-560 GPU-h (about 340-840 with contingency) plus 2,000-8,000 CPU core-h. The proposal as written would cost about 1,000-2,900 GPU-h, 11-33x the 85-90 GPU-h used so far. Using DFT barriers in TCAD needs ATLAS launches beyond 57 of 57, which requires the user's approval.
